# Model and source

```{r meta}
mod <- readModelDb("Huang_2026_busulfan")
cat(rxode2::rxode(mod)$reference)
```

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.2147/DDDT.S593835> (open access, PMC13401924)
* Supplementary material (Equations S1-S6, Tables S1-S6): the Word file
  linked from the article page.

Huang 2026 pooled 457 Chinese children from five transplant centres who
received intravenous busulfan four times daily for 3 days (Bu3) or 4 days
(Bu4) before allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). A
one-compartment population PK model gave each child's busulfan exposure: the
first-dose AUC (dose / individual CL) and the cumulative AUC over the course
(cAUC). The authors then related those exposures to event-free survival (EFS)
and to transplant complications with restricted cubic splines and Cox
proportional-hazards models.

The paper contributes six model files, all documented here:

| File | Content | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Huang_2026_busulfan` | Final popPK model | Table 1; Supplementary Equations S1-S6 |
| `Huang_2026_busulfan_efs` | EFS, all patients, first-dose AUC < 4.5 mg*h/L | Table S2a |
| `Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu3` | EFS, Bu3, cAUC < 54 mg*h/L | Table S2b |
| `Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu4` | EFS, Bu4, cAUC < 70 or > 90 mg*h/L | Table S2c |
| `Huang_2026_busulfan_nrm_bu3` | Nonrelapse mortality, Bu3, cAUC < 54 mg*h/L plus age band | Table S6 |
| `Huang_2026_busulfan_hc_bu3` | Grade 3-4 hemorrhagic cystitis, Bu3, cAUC < 54 mg*h/L | Table S4b |

The popPK model scales clearance and volume on a parameter-specific normal
fat mass (NFM), with separately estimated fat fractions for CL and V and
theory-based exponents of 3/4 and 1. A sigmoid maturation function of
postmenstrual age (PMA) acts on CL, children with slow GSTA1 metabolism clear
13.5% less, and CL carries between-occasion variability.

# Population

The PK model was fitted to 2,103 concentrations from 457 children (Results;
Table 1). Two children with less than 3 months of follow-up were left out of
the outcome analyses, leaving 455 (Table 2): median age 7.5 years (range
0.5-17.0), median weight 24.5 kg (5.0-96.5), 36.7% female, and 73.9% with a
malignant disease. 326 received the Bu3 regimen (median 8.6 years, 27.0 kg)
and 129 the Bu4 regimen (median 4.5 years, 17.0 kg). Busulfan was given at
0.8-1.2 mg/kg per dose (actual or adjusted body weight) as a 2 h infusion
every 6 h with no dose adjustment. Samples were taken 2, 4 and 6 h after the
start of the first infusion, with extra samples at 0.5, 1 and 2.5 h in some
children and repeat sampling around the fifth dose in others.

```{r population-metadata}
str(mod()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
table collects them, together with the equations in `model()`.

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `lcl` (CL_STD) | log(10.8 L/h) | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (V_STD) | log(46.4 L) | Table 1 |
| `ffat_cl` (Ffat_CL) | 1.08 | Table 1 |
| `ffat_v` (Ffat_V) | 0.653 | Table 1 |
| `e_nfm_cl` | 0.75, fixed | Supplementary Equation S3 |
| `e_nfm_vc` | 1, fixed | Supplementary Equation S4 |
| `tm50_mat` (TM50) | 41.6 weeks | Table 1 |
| `hill_mat` (HILL) | 3.42 | Table 1 |
| `e_gsta1_slow_cl` (FGSTA1_CL) | 0.865 | Table 1; Results "13.5% lower" |
| `etalcl` (BSV_CL) | 0.336^2 | Table 1; Results "33.6%" |
| `etalvc` (BSV_V) | 0.252^2 | Table 1; Results "25.2%" |
| `etaiov_cl_1..4` (BOV_CL) | 0.112^2 | Table 1; Results "11.2%" |
| `propSd` (RUV_PROP) | 0.178 | Table 1 |
| `addSd` (RUV_ADD) | 0.0312 mg/L | Table 1 |
| FFM = WHSmax x HT^2 x WT / (WHS50 x HT^2 + WT) | | Supplementary Equation S1 |
| NFM = FFM + Ffat x (WT - FFM) | | Supplementary Equation S2 |
| CL = CL_STD x (NFM / NFM_STD)^0.75 | | Supplementary Equation S3 |
| V = V_STD x NFM / NFM_STD | | Supplementary Equation S4 |
| Categorical covariate: P = P_STD x FCat | | Supplementary Equation S6 |
| Standard subject: 70 kg, 176 cm male, FFM_STD = 56.1 kg | | Table 1 footnote |
| Fmat = 1 / (1 + (PMA / TM50)^-HILL) | | Results (TM50, HILL); see Assumptions |
| `efs`: HR 1.63, AUC first < 4.5 mg*h/L | | Table S2a |
| `efs_bu3`: HR 1.73, cAUC3 days < 54 mg*h/L | | Table S2b |
| `efs_bu4`: HR 2.94 (< 70) and 3.22 (> 90) vs 70-90 mg*h/L | | Table S2c |
| `nrm_bu3`: HR 2.48 (cAUC3 days < 54); age 3-6, 6-12, > 12 vs 0-3 years: 0.39, 0.16, 0.40 | | Table S6 |
| `hc_bu3`: HR 0.38, cAUC3 days < 54 mg*h/L | | Table S4b |

The PK model takes `FFM` as a data column. The helper below implements
Supplementary Equation S1, which is how the paper computed it (height in
metres).

```{r ffm-helper}
ffm_janmahasatian <- function(WT, HT_cm, SEXF) {
  ht2 <- (HT_cm / 100)^2
  ifelse(
    SEXF == 1,
    37.99 * ht2 * WT / (35.98 * ht2 + WT),
    42.92 * ht2 * WT / (30.93 * ht2 + WT)
  )
}
# The standard subject: a 70 kg, 176 cm male has FFM 56.1 kg (Table 1 footnote).
ffm_std <- ffm_janmahasatian(70, 176, 0)
ffm_std
stopifnot(abs(ffm_std - 56.1) < 0.05)
```

# Closed-form checks

With all random effects at zero, the standard adult (70 kg, FFM 56.1 kg,
30 years old, born at term, rapid GSTA1 metabolizer) must return the Table 1
typical values; a slow metabolizer must have 0.865 times that clearance.

```{r closed-form}
typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
std_adult <- data.frame(
  id = rep(1:2, each = 2), time = rep(c(0, 1), 2), evid = rep(c(1, 0), 2),
  amt = rep(c(1, 0), 2), cmt = "central",
  WT = 70, FFM = 56.1, AGE = 30, GA = 40, GSTA1_RM = rep(c(1, 0), each = 2), OCC = 1
)
# One solve per subject: a multi-subject solve of a model with no omega warns.
s_std <- lapply(split(std_adult, std_adult$id), function(d) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(typ, d, returnType = "data.frame")
  cbind(id = d$id[1], s[nrow(s), c("cl", "vc", "fmat")])
}) |>
  bind_rows()
s_std |> select(id, cl, vc, fmat)
stopifnot(
  abs(s_std$fmat[1] - 1) < 1e-4,
  abs(s_std$cl[1] - 10.8 * s_std$fmat[1]) < 1e-6,
  abs(s_std$vc[1] - 46.4) < 1e-6,
  abs(s_std$cl[2] / s_std$cl[1] - 0.865) < 1e-9
)
```

Clearance reaches half its adult value at a PMA of 41.6 weeks. With a Hill
coefficient of 3.42, the youngest children in the cohort (0.5 years, about
66 weeks PMA) are already at about 83% of the adult value.

```{r maturation, fig.cap = "Maturation fraction of busulfan clearance against postmenstrual age (TM50 = 41.6 weeks, Hill = 3.42, Table 1). The dashed line marks 66 weeks, the PMA of a 0.5-year-old born at term, the youngest age in the cohort."}
pma <- seq(20, 400, by = 1)
fmat <- 1 / (1 + (pma / 41.6)^(-3.42))
ggplot(data.frame(pma, fmat), aes(pma, fmat)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5 * 52 + 40, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Postmenstrual age (weeks)", y = "Fraction of adult CL")
```

The standard NFM differs between CL and V, because the fat fraction does.
With Ffat_CL = 1.08 the clearance NFM is close to total body weight, while
V scales on FFM plus 65% of the fat mass.

```{r nfm-std}
c(
  nfm_std_cl = 56.1 + 1.08 * (70 - 56.1),
  nfm_std_v = 56.1 + 0.653 * (70 - 56.1)
)
```

# Virtual cohort

Two arms of 200 children mirror the Bu3 and Bu4 cohorts of Table 2. Ages are
drawn by the Table 2 age-band proportions, uniform within each band, and
truncated to 0.5-17 years. Height follows an approximate median
height-for-age curve and weight a body-mass index of about 16 kg/m^2, which
reproduces the median weights of Table 2. Sex follows Table 2. The paper does
not report how many children were rapid GSTA1 metabolizers, so 75% are
assumed to be (see Assumptions). All children were born at term.

Doses follow the weight bands of the EU busulfan label for children
(1.0 mg/kg below 9 kg, 1.2 mg/kg for 9-16 kg, 1.1 mg/kg for 16-23 kg,
0.95 mg/kg for 23-34 kg and 0.8 mg/kg above 34 kg). This spans the paper's
0.8-1.2 mg/kg range, but the paper does not state which dosing scheme each
centre used.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
n_arm <- 200

height_for_age <- function(age) {
  approx(
    x = c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 17),
    y = c(67, 76, 87, 96, 103, 110, 116, 128, 138, 149, 163, 170, 172),
    xout = age, rule = 2
  )$y
}
draw_age <- function(n, p_band) {
  band <- sample(1:4, n, replace = TRUE, prob = p_band)
  lo <- c(0.5, 3, 6, 12)[band]
  hi <- c(3, 6, 12, 17)[band]
  runif(n, lo, hi)
}
dose_mgkg <- function(WT) {
  cut(WT, c(0, 9, 16, 23, 34, Inf), right = FALSE, labels = FALSE) |>
    (\(i) c(1.0, 1.2, 1.1, 0.95, 0.8)[i])()
}

make_arm <- function(regimen, p_band, pct_female, id0) {
  tibble(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n_arm),
    regimen = regimen,
    AGE = draw_age(n_arm, p_band),
    SEXF = rbinom(n_arm, 1, pct_female / 100),
    GSTA1_RM = rbinom(n_arm, 1, 0.75),
    GA = 40
  )
}
cohort <- bind_rows(
  make_arm("Bu3", c(10.12, 22.39, 45.40, 22.09), 38.65, 0),
  make_arm("Bu4", c(39.53, 18.60, 29.46, 12.40), 31.78, n_arm)
) |>
  mutate(
    HT = height_for_age(AGE) * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.04)),
    WT = 16 * (HT / 100)^2 * exp(rnorm(n(), 0, 0.12)),
    FFM = ffm_janmahasatian(WT, HT, SEXF),
    dose = dose_mgkg(WT) * WT,
    n_days = ifelse(regimen == "Bu3", 3, 4)
  )

cohort |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `Median age (y)` = median(AGE),
    `Median weight (kg)` = median(WT),
    `Weight range (kg)` = paste(round(range(WT), 1), collapse = "-"),
    `Female (%)` = 100 * mean(SEXF),
    `Median dose (mg/kg)` = median(dose / WT)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort (compare Table 2: Bu3 median 8.6 y and 27.0 kg; Bu4 median 4.5 y and 17.0 kg).")
```

# Simulation

Each child receives a 2 h infusion every 6 h for 3 or 4 days. The occasion
(`OCC`) is the conditioning day. Concentrations are recorded every 15 min
from the first dose to 48 h after the last dose, so the AUC over the whole
course can be extrapolated to infinity.

```{r simulate}
doses <- cohort |>
  group_by(id) |>
  reframe(time = seq(0, by = 6, length.out = 4 * n_days)) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 1, amt = dose, dur = 2)
obs <- cohort |>
  group_by(id) |>
  reframe(time = seq(0, 24 * n_days + 48, by = 0.25)) |>
  left_join(cohort, by = "id") |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0)
ev <- bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = pmin(floor(time / 24) + 1, 4)) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, dur, cmt, WT, FFM, AGE, GA, GSTA1_RM, OCC) |>
  as.data.frame()

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, sim, cl, OCC) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, regimen), by = "id")
```

```{r vpc, fig.cap = "Simulated busulfan concentrations over the first dosing interval (median and 5th-95th percentiles, with residual error), by regimen. The paper sampled at 2, 4 and 6 h after the start of the first infusion; compare the prediction-corrected VPC in Figure 2 of Huang 2026."}
sim |>
  filter(time <= 6) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), p50 = median(sim), p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  labs(x = "Time after start of first infusion (h)", y = "Busulfan (mg/L)")
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper's exposures are the first-dose AUC (first dose / individual CL) and
the cumulative AUC (all doses / individual CL). For a linear model these are
the AUC from zero to infinity after a single first dose and after the whole
course. The course AUC comes from the multiple-dose simulation above. The
first-dose AUC needs a separate single-dose simulation of the same children,
sampled to 48 h.

```{r first-dose}
ev1 <- bind_rows(
  cohort |> mutate(time = 0, evid = 1, amt = dose, dur = 2),
  cohort |> tidyr::crossing(t = seq(0, 48, by = 0.25)) |>
    mutate(time = t, evid = 0, amt = 0, dur = 0) |>
    select(-t)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central", OCC = 1) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, dur, cmt, WT, FFM, AGE, GA, GSTA1_RM, OCC) |>
  as.data.frame()
sim1 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev1, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, cl) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, regimen), by = "id")
```

```{r pknca}
nca_run <- function(conc, dose_df, end) {
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
    conc |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, regimen, time, Cc),
    Cc ~ time | regimen + id
  )
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
dose_first <- cohort |> transmute(id, regimen, time = 0, amt = dose)
nca_first <- nca_run(sim1, dose_first)
# Only the first dose is passed to PKNCA so that the single 0-Inf interval
# integrates the whole multiple-dose profile.
nca_course <- nca_run(sim, dose_first)

auc_tbl <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_first$result) |> mutate(metric = "first"),
  as.data.frame(nca_course$result) |> mutate(metric = "course")
) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  select(id, regimen, metric, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = PPORRES)

# Cross-check against the paper's definition, dose / individual CL.
cl_tbl <- sim1 |>
  filter(time == 1) |>
  select(id, cl1 = cl) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, dose), by = "id")
auc_tbl <- auc_tbl |>
  left_join(cl_tbl, by = "id") |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, WT), by = "id") |>
  mutate(first_closed = dose / cl1, mgkg = dose / WT)
stopifnot(max(abs(auc_tbl$first / auc_tbl$first_closed - 1)) < 0.01)
```

The PKNCA first-dose AUC matches dose / CL to within 1% for every child, as it
must for a linear model sampled to 48 h.

The table compares the simulated medians with the Results.

```{r nca-compare}
sim_long <- bind_rows(
  auc_tbl |> transmute(id, exposure = "First dose, all patients", PPTESTCD = "aucinf.obs", PPORRES = first),
  auc_tbl |> transmute(id, exposure = paste0("Whole course (cAUC), ", regimen), PPTESTCD = "aucinf.obs", PPORRES = course)
)
ref <- data.frame(
  exposure = c("First dose, all patients", "Whole course (cAUC), Bu3", "Whole course (cAUC), Bu4"),
  aucinf.obs = c(4.5, 54.2, 70.5)
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_long[, c("exposure", "PPTESTCD", "PPORRES")],
  reference = ref,
  by = "exposure",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Median simulated busulfan exposure against the Results (first-dose AUC median 4.5 mg*h/L in all patients; cAUC median 54.2 mg*h/L for Bu3 and 70.5 mg*h/L for Bu4).")
```

Under this dosing the simulated medians sit about 15-25% above the paper's. The likely reason is the
assumed dosing rather than the model. The EU label bands give these children
a median of 0.95 mg/kg (Bu3) and 1.1 mg/kg (Bu4). At the lead centre, though,
112 of 128 children in the earlier `Du_2022_busulfan` cohort received
0.8 mg/kg. The paper reports only the 0.8-1.2 mg/kg range, so the real dose
mix lies somewhere between "0.8 mg/kg for everyone" and the EU bands.

Because the model is linear, each child's AUC at 0.8 mg/kg follows exactly by
rescaling. The check below asks whether each published median falls between
the two dosing scenarios, with 10% slack at each end for the approximate body
sizes. A clearance mis-scaled by 20% or more would move both scenarios past
the published value.

```{r dose-bracket}
bracket <- auc_tbl |>
  mutate(first_08 = first * 0.8 / mgkg, course_08 = course * 0.8 / mgkg)
bracket_tbl <- tibble(
  Exposure = c("First-dose AUC, all patients", "cAUC, Bu3", "cAUC, Bu4"),
  Published = c(4.5, 54.2, 70.5),
  dose_08 = c(
    median(bracket$first_08),
    median(bracket$course_08[bracket$regimen == "Bu3"]),
    median(bracket$course_08[bracket$regimen == "Bu4"])
  ),
  dose_eu = c(
    median(bracket$first),
    median(bracket$course[bracket$regimen == "Bu3"]),
    median(bracket$course[bracket$regimen == "Bu4"])
  )
)
bracket_tbl |>
  rename(
    "Published median (mg*h/L)" = Published,
    "Simulated, 0.8 mg/kg for all" = dose_08,
    "Simulated, EU label bands" = dose_eu
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median busulfan AUC under the two dosing scenarios against the Results.")
stopifnot(
  all(bracket_tbl$Published >= 0.9 * pmin(bracket_tbl$dose_08, bracket_tbl$dose_eu)),
  all(bracket_tbl$Published <= 1.1 * pmax(bracket_tbl$dose_08, bracket_tbl$dose_eu))
)
```

The paper's AUCs are empirical-Bayes estimates for real children. The full
ranges in the Results (first-dose AUC 1.8-10.5, Bu3 cAUC 26.5-119.0, Bu4 cAUC
30.2-109.9 mg*h/L) can be set against the simulated 2.5th-97.5th percentiles
under the EU-band dosing:

```{r auc-range}
auc_tbl |>
  pivot_longer(c(first, course), names_to = "metric") |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(metric == "first", "All patients, first dose", paste(regimen, "cAUC"))) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    p2.5 = quantile(value, 0.025), median = median(value), p97.5 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated busulfan AUC (mg*h/L), 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles.")
```

# Exposure-response models

## The published hazard ratios are reproduced exactly

The five Cox models are algebraic and deterministic, so their output can be
checked against the printed hazard ratios to the printed precision. Each
evaluation uses one subject with one observation row per covariate value.

```{r hr-eval}
er_eval <- function(name, covs) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_len(nrow(covs)), amt = 0, evid = 0L) |>
    bind_cols(covs)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(name), events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(covs))
  s$hr
}

hr_efs <- er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_FIRST = c(5, 4.5, 4.49)))
hr_efs_bu3 <- er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu3", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = c(60, 54, 53.9)))
hr_efs_bu4 <- er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu4", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = c(80, 70, 90, 69.9, 90.1)))
hr_nrm <- er_eval(
  "Huang_2026_busulfan_nrm_bu3",
  data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = c(60, 50, 60, 60, 60), AGE = c(2, 2, 4, 8, 14))
)
hr_hc <- er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_hc_bu3", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = c(60, 50)))

hr_check <- tibble(
  Model = c(
    "efs", "efs", "efs_bu3", "efs_bu3", "efs_bu4", "efs_bu4", "efs_bu4", "efs_bu4",
    "nrm_bu3", "nrm_bu3", "nrm_bu3", "nrm_bu3", "hc_bu3"
  ),
  Contrast = c(
    "AUC first = 4.5 (reference edge)", "AUC first < 4.5",
    "cAUC = 54 (reference edge)", "cAUC < 54",
    "cAUC = 70 (reference edge)", "cAUC = 90 (reference edge)", "cAUC < 70", "cAUC > 90",
    "cAUC < 54, age 0-3", "cAUC >= 54, age 3-6", "cAUC >= 54, age 6-12", "cAUC >= 54, age > 12",
    "cAUC < 54"
  ),
  Published = c(1, 1.63, 1, 1.73, 1, 1, 2.94, 3.22, 2.48, 0.39, 0.16, 0.40, 0.38),
  Model_hr = c(
    hr_efs[2], hr_efs[3], hr_efs_bu3[2], hr_efs_bu3[3],
    hr_efs_bu4[2], hr_efs_bu4[3], hr_efs_bu4[4], hr_efs_bu4[5],
    hr_nrm[2], hr_nrm[3], hr_nrm[4], hr_nrm[5], hr_hc[2]
  )
)
hr_check |>
  rename("Model HR" = Model_hr, "Published HR" = Published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Hazard ratios from the packaged models against Tables S2a, S2b, S2c, S6 and S4b (multivariate columns).")
# Same parameters on both sides, so the agreement is exact.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(hr_check$Model_hr - hr_check$Published) < 1e-9),
  hr_efs[1] == 1, hr_efs_bu3[1] == 1, hr_efs_bu4[1] == 1, hr_nrm[1] == 1, hr_hc[1] == 1
)
```

## Exposure groups in the simulated cohort

The cut points split the paper's cohorts into groups of known size (Tables
S2a-S2c). Feeding the simulated exposures through the same cut points checks
the PK model and the assumed dosing together: a mis-scaled clearance would
shift every group share.

```{r groups}
group_shares <- function(d, first_col, course_col) {
  d <- d |> mutate(f = .data[[first_col]], c = .data[[course_col]])
  bind_rows(
    d |> transmute(Analysis = "All, AUC first", Group = ifelse(f < 4.5, "< 4.5", ">= 4.5")),
    d |> filter(regimen == "Bu3") |>
      transmute(Analysis = "Bu3, cAUC", Group = ifelse(c < 54, "< 54", ">= 54")),
    d |> filter(regimen == "Bu4") |>
      transmute(
        Analysis = "Bu4, cAUC",
        Group = case_when(c < 70 ~ "< 70", c > 90 ~ "> 90", TRUE ~ "70-90")
      )
  ) |>
    count(Analysis, Group) |>
    group_by(Analysis) |>
    mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    select(-n)
}
grp_pub <- tibble(
  Analysis = c("All, AUC first", "All, AUC first", "Bu3, cAUC", "Bu3, cAUC", "Bu4, cAUC", "Bu4, cAUC", "Bu4, cAUC"),
  Group = c(">= 4.5", "< 4.5", ">= 54", "< 54", "70-90", "< 70", "> 90"),
  pub_pct = c(50.77, 49.23, 50.92, 49.08, 34.88, 46.51, 18.60)
)
grp <- grp_pub |>
  left_join(group_shares(bracket, "first_08", "course_08") |> rename(pct_08 = pct), by = c("Analysis", "Group")) |>
  left_join(group_shares(bracket, "first", "course") |> rename(pct_eu = pct), by = c("Analysis", "Group")) |>
  mutate(pct_08 = coalesce(pct_08, 0), pct_eu = coalesce(pct_eu, 0))
grp |>
  rename(
    "Published (%)" = pub_pct,
    "Simulated, 0.8 mg/kg for all (%)" = pct_08,
    "Simulated, EU label bands (%)" = pct_eu
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Share of patients in each exposure group: Tables S2a-S2c against the simulated cohort under the two dosing scenarios.")
# For the two dichotomies, the published below-cut share should fall between
# the two dosing scenarios, with 10 percentage points of slack.
below <- grp |> filter(Group %in% c("< 4.5", "< 54"))
stopifnot(
  all(below$pub_pct >= pmin(below$pct_08, below$pct_eu) - 10),
  all(below$pub_pct <= pmax(below$pct_08, below$pct_eu) + 10)
)
```

## Relative hazard across the simulated cohort

Because the baseline hazards are not reported, the models return hazards
relative to each analysis' reference group. Applied to the simulated cohort,
they give each child's EFS hazard multiplier.

```{r hr-cohort, fig.cap = "Relative EFS hazard against simulated busulfan exposure: first-dose AUC for all patients (Table S2a) and cumulative AUC by regimen (Tables S2b and S2c). Dashed lines mark the cut points."}
hr_all <- er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_FIRST = auc_tbl$first))
bu3 <- auc_tbl |> filter(regimen == "Bu3")
bu4 <- auc_tbl |> filter(regimen == "Bu4")
hr_plot <- bind_rows(
  tibble(panel = "All patients: first-dose AUC", auc = auc_tbl$first, hr = hr_all),
  tibble(
    panel = "Bu3: cAUC", auc = bu3$course,
    hr = er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu3", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = bu3$course))
  ),
  tibble(
    panel = "Bu4: cAUC", auc = bu4$course,
    hr = er_eval("Huang_2026_busulfan_efs_bu4", data.frame(AUC_BUSULFAN_COURSE = bu4$course))
  )
)
cuts <- tibble(
  panel = c("All patients: first-dose AUC", "Bu3: cAUC", "Bu4: cAUC", "Bu4: cAUC"),
  x = c(4.5, 54, 70, 90)
)
ggplot(hr_plot, aes(auc, hr)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_vline(data = cuts, aes(xintercept = x), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Busulfan AUC (mg*h/L)", y = "Relative hazard of an EFS event")
```

## Published Kaplan-Meier estimates

The 2-year EFS rates by exposure group (Figure 4 and Results) are listed for
reference. They are **published values, not model predictions**: the Cox
models carry no baseline hazard, so they cannot produce absolute survival.

| Analysis | Group | 2-year EFS (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| All patients | AUC first >= 4.5 mg*h/L | 84.6% |
| All patients | AUC first < 4.5 mg*h/L | 76.4% |
| Bu3 | cAUC >= 54 mg*h/L | 86.4% (80.11-90.86) |
| Bu3 | cAUC < 54 mg*h/L | 77.7% (70.36-83.49) |
| Bu4 | cAUC 70-90 mg*h/L | 88.9% (75.34-95.22) |
| Bu4 | cAUC < 70 mg*h/L | 71.0% (57.57-80.93) |
| Bu4 | cAUC > 90 mg*h/L | 66.1% (43.42-81.44) |

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference NFM.** Supplementary Equations S3 and S4 divide NFM by
  NFM_STD, which the paper does not print. It is read as the NFM of the
  stated standard subject (70 kg, 176 cm male, FFM_STD 56.1 kg) with each
  parameter's own fat fraction: 71.1 kg for CL and 65.2 kg for V. This makes
  CL_STD and V_STD the values for that standard subject, as the Table 1
  footnote says, and matches the same group's earlier busulfan model
  (`Du_2022_busulfan`). The supplement's sentence giving 56.1 kg as the
  "standard fat mass" is read as FFM_STD, the value the Table 1 footnote
  gives for the same subject.
* **Maturation function and PMA.** The paper reports TM50 and HILL but does
  not print the maturation equation or how PMA was derived. The standard
  sigmoid Fmat = 1 / (1 + (PMA / TM50)^-HILL) is used, as in
  `Du_2022_busulfan`, with PMA (weeks) = AGE x 52 + GA. Gestational age was
  not reported; use 40 weeks when unknown. In this age range (0.5-17 years)
  a few weeks of GA barely change Fmat.
* **GSTA1 coding.** The paper splits GSTA1 diplotypes into rapid and slow
  (intermediate plus poor) metabolizers following Ben Hassine 2021. This is
  the register's `GSTA1_RM` (1 = rapid). The paper's reference group is
  rapid, so CL is multiplied by 0.865 when `GSTA1_RM = 0`; the coefficient is
  not inverted. The share of rapid metabolizers is not reported. The virtual
  cohort assumes 75%, near the share of the *A/*A diplotype in a cohort from
  the same centre (Yuan 2021).
* **Variability scale.** BSV_CL 0.336, BSV_V 0.252 and BOV_CL 0.112
  (Results: 33.6%, 25.2%, 11.2%) are read as the SD of eta, as in
  `Du_2022_busulfan`. Reading them as CVs (omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1)) would
  lower the variances by 3-5%.
* **Occasions.** The paper reports BOV on CL but does not define an
  occasion. Sampling was around the first and fifth doses, so the model
  takes the conditioning day as the occasion (`OCC` 1-4). Records with `OCC`
  outside 1-4 have no BOV. rxode2 has no NONMEM-style occasion level, so the
  four occasion etas are selected by indicators, which rxode2 cannot
  mu-reference; it warns "some etas defaulted to non-mu referenced" on every
  solve. The warning affects only estimation speed-ups, not simulation.
* **Residual error.** The paper gives a proportional (17.8%) and an additive
  (0.0312 mg/L) term without the combination rule; the nlmixr2 default
  `add() + prop()` (variances add) is used.
* **Dosing in the virtual cohort.** The paper reports only the
  0.8-1.2 mg/kg range. The simulation uses the EU label weight bands, and a
  second scenario rescales every child to 0.8 mg/kg, the dose most children
  at the lead centre received in `Du_2022_busulfan`. The published exposure
  medians and group shares are checked to lie between the two scenarios. The
  dosing assumption affects the simulated AUCs but not the model.
* **Exposure-response models.** The Cox models are semiparametric, so no
  baseline hazard exists to extract; the files return relative hazards only.
  The cut points (4.5, 54, 70 and 90 mg*h/L) were read off restricted cubic
  splines rather than estimated, and are encoded as fixed. For the 4-day
  regimen the reference window is taken as 70 <= cAUC <= 90 mg*h/L. In the
  NRM model, ages on a band edge are put in the higher band (3 and 6 years),
  except 12 years, which stays in 6-12. The Cox models for aGVHD, oral
  mucositis and grade 2-4 hemorrhagic cystitis (Tables S3a-S3b, S4a, S4c,
  S5a-S5b) contain no busulfan exposure term and are not encoded. The
  restricted cubic spline curves of Figure 3 are shown only as figures, with
  no coefficients, and are not encoded either.
* **Overlap with earlier models.** The cohort includes patients from the
  single-centre studies behind `Du_2022_busulfan` and `Yuan_2021_busulfan`.
  The present model is a separate, larger fit and does not replace them.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction for this article was found (checked
  2026-11-14).
